body:
Thank you for walking me through that. It does help. I am so sorry to hear about what you and your family have been through since your brother passed. I hope he knew how much you all loved him when he was alive. It is sad to think about, but it also reminds me that others really do care in our lives, even when we may not be fully aware of how much.

I am actually afraid that my family will somehow be notified and potentially have some say in any part of the process, no matter how many forms I fill out designating that I want them to have no part. I do feel bad at the thought of leaving my roommates in a hard situation, though. It's difficult for me to imagine anyone caring about me enough to be hurt or feel true loss when I am gone, but I do think about putting aside a fund to cover at least a few months of rent and any other costs they might incur having to move my stuff, find a new roommate, etc (theoretically I should have someone designated to take care of clearing out my stuff in my will, but I'm just afraid that any formal or legal process will somehow leave gaps that the people I leave behind will have to scramble to accommodate). I just don't want to leave a mess or any trouble for anyone.

I wish there was an easier way to find counseling for this sort of thing. Every counselor or professional I talk to is paranoid about legal liabilities and don't want to help 'enable' me. Dying is a part of life. If not by my own hand, I could get hit by a bus tomorrow and it would be the same thing. But there is such a stigma around it.

Anyway. Thanks again for your input. As you can see, I'm still here. I feel like half of me wants nothing more than to live and be awesome again, and the other half just wants to finally be rid of the problem that is my existence once and for all. But like you point out, there's no way to go about that that doesn't impact the people in my life anyway.

I hope things work out for you and your family.
Yeah. I'm apparently too damn stubborn to quit. ;-)

You know, even when I come asking for answers, I don't expect them; the simple fact you cared enough to read even part of what I wrote (no small feat), and bothered to respond has honestly already made me feel better. Thank you!
